title: The Story about the Young Sow
synopsis: One day the Buddha saw a sow and smiled; when Elder Ānanda asked him the reason for his smile he told of the various forms of existence that the sow had been through, including being reborn in the Brahma worlds in the life before this one; he then taught the monastics on the wickedness of craving with some verses. Atimbara, King Duṭṭhagāmaṇī, Elder Anula, Elder Mahā Tissa
verse_english: Dhp 338: Just as when the root remains firm and untroubled though the tree was cut down, it grows again, so when the tendency to craving is not rooted out this suffering appears again and again. / Dhp 339: He in whom the thirty-six streams flow pleasantly and strong, the one with wrong view, is carried away by his passionate intentions. / Dhp 340: Streams are flowing everywhere, the creepers remain where they grow, seeing this, cut the creeper’s root that has arisen with wisdom. / Dhp 341: * There are flowing streams of affection and mental happinesses for a person, pleasure-dependent they seek happiness, those people undergo both birth and old age. / Dhp 342: People surrounded by craving crawl round like a hare in a trap, attached and clinging to fetters they come back again and again to suffering for a long time. / Dhp 343: People surrounded by craving crawl round like a hare in a trap, therefore he should remove craving – the monk who longs for dispassion for himself.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Culla Sāri
synopsis: Elder Culla Sāri gave medical treatment to others in exchange for a portion of food, which is against the right ways of earning his livelihood as laid down by the Buddha; when the Buddha heard of his behaviour he gave a teaching in some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 244: Life is light for one without shame, with the bold courage of a crow, living a life with backbiting, recklessness, and defilements. / Dhp 245: Life is hard when endowed with shame, for the one constantly seeking purity, for one sincere, and not reckless, looking for purity of life.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about a Company of Old Elders
synopsis: Some laymen heard the Buddha teaching and ordained in old age, but even after ordaining they still visited their families for meals; when a former wife of one of them died they fell into deep lamentation; the Buddha explained they did that also in previous lives as crows, and gave the bhikkhus a teaching with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 283: Cut down the forest (of defilements) not just a tree, from the forest arises a danger, having cut down the forest and thicket, you should be without forests, monastics. / Dhp 284: * For as long as an atom of desire of a man for a woman is not cut down, for just so long is the mind in bondage, like a calf (in bondage) to mother’s milk.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse. Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Kokālika
verse_english: Dhp 17: Here he suffers, after death he suffers, the wicked one suffers in both places, he suffers, thinking: “I have done wickedness,” gone to a bad fate, he suffers much more.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Aṅkura
synopsis: Aṅkura was a good Brahmin who set up many fire places and worshipped the gods for ten thousand years, yet his position in the heavens was less than Indaka who gave just one spoonful of rice to Elder Anuruddha; the Buddha explained with some verses that one should give with discrimination, as gifts given to those who are free of defilements yield great fruit.
verse_english: Dhp 356: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by passion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without passion. / Dhp 357: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by hatred, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without hatred. / Dhp 358: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by delusion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without delusion. / Dhp 359: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by desire, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without desire.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Three Groups
synopsis: Three different groups of bhikkhus who were on their way to the Buddha saw a crow die in mid-air, a woman drowned on a voyage and themselves get buried in a cave; they asked the Buddha why it all happened, and he explained there is nowhere to escape from the results of bad actions, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 127: Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor after entering a mountain cleft: there is no place found on this earth where one can be free from (the results of) wicked deeds.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about the Elder Upananda the Sakyan
synopsis: Elder Upananda taught well, but was a greedy bhikkhu who always took the biggest offering, one day he swindled two bhikkhus out of a blanket, and the Buddha explained that one should train oneself before teaching to others, and summarised his teaching with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 158: First one should establish oneself in what is suitable, then one can advise another, the wise one should not have (any) defilement.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta taught on generosity and people decided to give alms; one man gave a robe, which they decided to give to Elder Devadatta; when the Buddha heard about it he related a Birth Story about Devadatta, who, as an elephant hunter, disguised himself as a Paccekabuddha in order to kill his prey, and then spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 9: The one who, while still impure, would wear the renunciant’s robe, unendowed with restraint and truth, is not worthy of the renunciant’s robe. / Dhp 10: The one who, steady in virtue, throws out (any) impurity, endowed with restraint and truth, is indeed worthy of the renunciant’s robe.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about the Elder Cittahattha
synopsis: Cittahattha wavered continually between being a bhikkhu and a householder, but eventually he saw into the truth of impermanence, ordained yet again and became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 38: For the one with unsettled mind, who does not know the True Dhamma, whose confidence is wavering, wisdom is unfulfilled. / Dhp 39: For the one with mind free of lust, for the one with mind unperplexed, for the one who has abandoned making merit and demerit, for the watchful, there is no fear.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
synopsis: A bhikkhu was given a meditation subject but could make no progress, so he determined to return to the Buddha; on his way he saw a great fire burn down a forest, and the Buddha appeared to him and taught him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 31: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in heedlessness, advances like burning fire against the fetter, small or large.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about Nephew Saṅgharakkhita
synopsis: Saṅgharakkhita ordained as a bhikkhu and received robes, one of which he wished to give to an elder, his uncle; the elder had no need for it though and refused it; Elder Saṅgharakkhita daydreamed about returning to the household life, and was distressed when his daydream was exposed, and the Buddha taught him in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 37: * Those who will restrain the mind that roams far, is lonesome, without a body, hidden, gain release from the bonds of Māra.

title: The Story about the Elder Nanda
synopsis: The Buddha’s half-brother Nanda ordained, but yearned for the lay-life; the Buddha promised him celestial maidens as a reward for his efforts in the spiritual life; Nanda put forth effort and became an Arahat, and the Buddha was released from his promise; these verses were spoken about him. Lives
verse_english: Dhp 13: Just as the rain penetrates a house with thatching that is poor, so passion penetrates a mind that is undeveloped. / Dhp 14: Just as rain does not penetrate a house with thatching that is good, so passion cannot penetrate a mind that is well-developed.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about the Fruits and Powers of People’s Bad Conduct
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna saw a Peta dressed as a bhikkhu flying through the air with body all on fire and reported it to the Buddha, who told that previously the Peta had been a bhikkhu under Buddha Kassapa, but had not lived accordingly, and then he spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 307: Many wearing the monastic robe around their necks are wicked, unrestrained, the wicked through their wicked deeds re-arisein the underworld.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the One Who Honoured Her Husband
synopsis: Patipūjikā passed away from heaven and was reborn on earth, had four sons, served the monastics faithfully, and at the end of her life was reunited with her husband Mālabhārī in Tāvatiṁsa Heaven; the monastics told the Buddha about the loss of their benefactor, and he gave this teaching.
verse_english: Dhp 48: * The End-Maker takes control of the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, even though he is unsated with sense pleasures.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the Young Brahmin Girl Ciñcā
synopsis: The young brahmin girl Ciñcā falsely accused the Buddha of impregnating her; the gods helped reveal the lie, and Ciñcā fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha explained the matter with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 176: For the person speaking falsely, who has transgressed in this one thing, who has abandoned the next world, there is no wickedness left undone.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about Nandiya
synopsis: The faithful householder Nandiya erected a building at Isipatana for the monastics and as he poured the water of donation a celestial mansion arose for him in the Realm of the Thirty-Three gods; Elder Moggallāna saw it and asked the Buddha about it, who explained the matter with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 219: When one who lives abroad for a long time comes safely from afar, his relatives, friends and companions come and greatly rejoice. / Dhp 220: Just so, when one who has performed merit goes from this world unto the next, his merits are received just as relatives come to their loved one.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa’s Pupil
synopsis: A faithless pupil of Elder Mahā Kassapa, after numerous other acts of deceit, tricked a supporter into giving him food and drinks which he said were needed by the elder; after being rebuked he burned down the elder’s hut, ran away and was later reborn in Avīci, the relentless hell; the Buddha then gave some advice in verse.
verse_english: Dhp 61: If while roaming one cannot find one better or the same as oneself, one should resolve to go alone: there is no friendship with fools.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the Yakkhinī Kāḷi
synopsis: A barren woman brings home a young woman for her husband, but every time the young wife conceives the barren wife contrives an abortion; through life after life they consume each other’s children, until brought to the Buddha, who taught them with a verse. named, Elder Ānanda, Deva Sumana
verse_english: Dhp 5: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place, they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is (surely) eternal.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the Elder Soreyya
synopsis: A merchant’s son, Soreyya, developed lust for Elder Mahā Kaccāyana and was transformed into a woman; later, after asking pardon, he became a man again, ordained and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha explained what a well-directed mind can do for one.
verse_english: Dhp 43: Mother and father might not do for him, or other relatives, as much good as a mind that is well-directed can do for him.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about a Certain Youth of Good Family
synopsis: A youth got married but his wife was given to adultery and put the young man to shame; when he met the Buddha the latter reminded him that in a previous existence also he was betrayed by his wife, and then he taught him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 242: Bad conduct is a woman’s stain, stinginess is a giver’s stain, wicked actions are indeed stains both in this world and in the next. / Dhp 243: A stain that is worse than that stain, ignorance is the supreme stain, after abandoning that stain, be without stains, O monastics!

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about a Woman Who Ate Chicken Eggs
synopsis: A young girl stole a hen’s eggs, and the hen, when reborn killed the girl’s offspring; through their hateful connection they were reborn together and destroyed each other’s children in five hundred existences; when the Buddha met them he taught them with a verse, and their hatreds were appeased.
verse_english: Dhp 291: One who desires happiness for oneself by causing suffering for another, being associated thus with hatred, is not fully released from that hatred.

title: The Story about Viḍūḍabha
synopsis: Prince Viḍūḍabha learned that he was the son of a Sakyan slave-woman due to a trick the Sakyans had played on his father, King Pasenadi, and he vowed revenge; on becoming king he massacred the Sakyans, but on his way home he and his army were swept away by flood waters; later the Buddha spoke a verse summarising what had happened. Moggallāna, Ānanda, Kesava, Kappa, Nārada, Mahānāma, Vāsabhā Khattiyā, Mallikā, Dīgha Kārāyaṇa
verse_english: Dhp 47: * Death takes up and carries away the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, like a great flood (carries off) a sleeping village.

question: In a past-life tale, a woman so attached to money comes back as a small animal living on top of the hoard. Which story?
title: The Story about the Mother of Kāṇā
synopsis: Kāṇā resented and reviled the bhikkhus for taking cakes she wanted to offer to her husband; but the Buddha showed they had only taken what was offered, and she gained faith and attained Stream-entry; the Buddha explained she had also been offended in a past life, and then spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 82: Like a lake that is deep, clear and unruffled, just so the wise are confident after listening to Dhamma.

title: The Story about the Twin Miracle
synopsis: After spending his seventh Rains Retreat teaching the Abhidhamma in the Realm of the Thirty-Three, the Buddha descended on a staircase built by Sakka, the Lord of the Devas, and Elder Sāriputta praised the Buddha in his glory; the Buddha explained the matter by reciting a verse. Bimbisāra, King Pasenadi Kosala, Sakka, Gaṇḍa, Elder Ānanda, Devaputta Vātavalāhaka, Devaputta Sun, Pūraṇa Kassapa, Gharaṇī, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Mahā Brahma, Sāmaṇerī Cīrā, Sāmaṇera Cunda, Bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, Nandivisāla, Elder Anuruddha, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Deva Indaka, Deva Aṅkura, Buddha Kassapa, Deva Pañcasikha, Mātali the charioteer, Suyāma Lives, Previous Buddhas, Bodhisatta
verse_english: Dhp 181: Those wise ones intent on meditation, who delight in the peace of renunciation, even the gods are envious of them, the Sambuddhas, the ones who are mindful.

question: In a past-life tale, a woman so attached to money comes back as a small animal living on top of the hoard. Which story?
title: The Story about the Old Brahmin’s Sons
synopsis: Some children who were previously negligent later gave a meal to the Buddha and the Saṅgha, and related how they now took care of their father; the Buddha recited a Birth Story relating how he too had cared for his parents, and spoke a verse showing how he would not eat until he was allowed to attend to his duties.
verse_english: Dhp 324: The tusker named Dhanapālaka musty in rut, difficult to restrain, bound, he doesn’t eat (even) a morsel, the tusker remembers the elephant forest.

question: In a past-life tale, a woman so attached to money comes back as a small animal living on top of the hoard. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Candābha
synopsis: Because of a past deed a light shone from the torso of the boy Candābha and he was taken round the country giving blessings; when he entered into the presence of the Buddha, however, the light disappeared; he then ordained and soon became an Arahat; the bhikkhus doubted his attainment and asked the Buddha, who spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 413: (Whoever) just like the moon is stainless, pure, clear and undisturbed, has destroyed joy in existence, that one I say is a brahmin.

question: In a past-life tale, a woman so attached to money comes back as a small animal living on top of the hoard. Which story?
title: The Story about the Prison House
synopsis: Some bhikkhus while on almsround saw various criminals in the prison house where they were bound with ropes and chains; they reported it to the Buddha who explained that these bonds are paltry compared to the bonds of craving, and he taught them further with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 345: That bondage is not so strong say the wise, that is made of iron or wood or reeds, * impassioned and excited they seek out jewels and earrings and children and wives – / Dhp 346: that bondage is strong say the wise, dragging down the lax, hard to get free from, having cut this down they wander about seeking nothing, abandoning the happiness in pleasure.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about the Lay Disciple Mahā Kāla
synopsis: The householder Mahā Kāla listened to an all-night Dhamma teaching at Jetavana, but in the morning was beaten to death by people who mistook him for a thief; the Buddha explained that he had caused the unjust death of another in a previous life, and his bad deed had caught up with him, and gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 161: That wickedness done by oneself, born in oneself, arising in oneself, crushes the one who is stupid, as a diamond (crushes) a rock-jewel.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about Those from Kosambī
synopsis: Parallels: Ja 428; Vin Mv 10.1-5; Ud 4.5; Ja 37124 The followers of two bhikkhus of Kosambī fell into a dispute and despite the Buddha’s admonitions, refused to be reconciled; the Buddha went forth to Pārileyyaka forest and was served by an elephant and a monkey; meanwhile the lay people refused to attend on the bhikkhus till they came to their senses; eventually they asked for forgiveness and the Buddha taught them with a verse. Kosala, Prince Dīghāvu, Bālaka, Elder Bhagu, Anāthapiṇḍika, Visākhā
verse_english: Dhp 6: The others do not understand that we should restrain ourselves here, but (for) those here who do understand, through that, (their) dissensions will cease.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍadhāna
synopsis: Elder Kuṇḍadhāna was followed round by a Devatā due to his behaviour in a previous existence, and the bhikkhus, thinking he was breaking his vow of chastity, incited the king to drive him out; the king believed in his innocence though and gave him an invitation; the bhikkhus blamed Elder Kuṇḍadhāna and he, unjustly, blamed them in return; the Buddha admonished him thus. Buddhas
verse_english: Dhp 133: Do not say anything harsh, spoken to they might answer back to you, for arrogant talk entails misery, and they might strike you back with a stick. / Dhp 134: If you make no sound like a gong that is broken, you are (like) one who has attained Nibbāna, contention is not found in you.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about Speaking and Rousing Oneself
synopsis: Queen Māgandiyā, who had been rejected by the Buddha, bribed the crowd and slaves to abuse him and the bhikkhus when they came to town; Elder Ānanda urged the Buddha to go elsewhere but the Buddha answered that they should be resolute and spoke about himself in these verses.
verse_english: Dhp 320: Like an elephant in battle (endures) an arrow shot from bow (so) will I endure abuse, for many people are unvirtuous. / Dhp 321: They lead one trained into a crowd, a king mounts one who has been trained, amongst humans one trained is best, the one who can endure abuse. / Dhp 322: Noble are the well-trained horses, the well-bred horses from Sindh, and the great tusker elephants, (and even) more noble than that is the one who has trained himself.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about a Company of Bhikkhus
synopsis: Owing to the Kosambī bhikkhus falling into an argument, the Buddha went to Pārileyyaka forest and was served by an elephant; after the Rains Retreat Elder Ānanda, being urged by the great disciples, went to invite the Buddha to return to Sāvatthi; the Buddha explained that he had a good companion in the elephant, but without such-like it is better to live alone, and he spoke some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 328: If you should find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, overcoming all your troubles you should live with that one, glad and mindful. / Dhp 329: If you do not find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, like a king who abandons his conquered kingdom one should live alone like a solitary elephant in the forest. / Dhp 330: It is better to live alone, there can be no friendship with a fool, one should live alone and not do anything bad, unconcerned like a solitary elephant in the forest.

verse_english: Dhp 47: * Death takes up and carries away the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, like a great flood (carries off) a sleeping village.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about the Bhikkhus Who Lived on the Banks of the Vaggumudā
synopsis: The bhikkhus who lived on the banks of the Vaggumudā went around praising each other and saying they had attained states they had not in order to get better almsfood; the Buddha restrained those bhikkhus and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 308: It’s better to have eaten a glowing iron ball, like a flame of fire, than that (the monastic) who is unrestrained and unvirtuous should enjoy the country’s almsfood.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about Prince Bodhi
synopsis: Prince Bodhi invited the Buddha for the first meal in his new palace, and put down cloth thinking if the Buddha stepped on it he would be blessed with children; the Buddha refused to walk on it, and explained that Prince Bodhi would be without children because of a past life in which he failed to protect himself by keeping precepts during any of the three periods of his life, and he then gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 157: If one regards oneself as dear one should guard oneself right well, during one of the three watches (of the night) the wise one should stay alert.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Prison House
synopsis: Some bhikkhus while on almsround saw various criminals in the prison house where they were bound with ropes and chains; they reported it to the Buddha who explained that these bonds are paltry compared to the bonds of craving, and he taught them further with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 345: That bondage is not so strong say the wise, that is made of iron or wood or reeds, * impassioned and excited they seek out jewels and earrings and children and wives – / Dhp 346: that bondage is strong say the wise, dragging down the lax, hard to get free from, having cut this down they wander about seeking nothing, abandoning the happiness in pleasure.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about a Company of Bhikkhus
synopsis: After Soṇa Kūṭikaṇṇa received ordination he recited Dhamma to the Buddha who praised him for it, which also caused the Devas to rejoice; on hearing about it, Soṇa’s mother invited her son to teach her Dhamma also, and wouldn’t leave the teaching even when she heard nine hundred thieves had broken into her house; seeing her piety, the thieves converted and went forth; this is the teaching the Buddha gave at that time.
verse_english: Dhp 368: That monastic who dwells in loving-kindness, with faith in Buddha’s dispensation, should attain the state of peace, the joy in stilling of (all) conditions. / Dhp 369: Please bail out this boat, monastic, when bailed out it will go lightly, cutting off passion and hatred, from here one will go to Nibbāna. / Dhp 370: One should cut off five, one should abandon five, one should cultivate five more, the monastic who surmounts five attachments is called a flood-crosser. / Dhp 371: Meditate, monastic, do not be heedless, do not let your mind swirl around in strands of desire, do not, heedless, swallow a (hot) iron ball, do not, while burning, cry: ‘This is suffering.’ / Dhp 372: There is no concentration for one without wisdom, there is no wisdom for one without concentration, the one who has both concentration and wisdom is indeed in the presence of Nibbāna. / Dhp 373: For the one who has entered an empty place, a monastic with a peaceful mind, there is superhuman delight from insight into true Dhamma. / Dhp 374: Whoever has right mindfulness regarding the rise and fall of the components (of mind and body) gains joy and happiness, that is the deathless state for the one who knows. / Dhp 375: This is the very beginning for the wise monastic here: contentment, guarding the senses, and restraint in the regulations. / Dhp 376: One should resort to spiritual friends, ones of pure life, ones who are diligent, one should be of friendly disposition, one who will be skilful in his conduct, rejoicing frequently because of that, one will make an end to suffering.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Upananda the Sakyan
synopsis: Elder Upananda taught well, but was a greedy bhikkhu who always took the biggest offering, one day he swindled two bhikkhus out of a blanket, and the Buddha explained that one should train oneself before teaching to others, and summarised his teaching with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 158: First one should establish oneself in what is suitable, then one can advise another, the wise one should not have (any) defilement.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse. Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Kokālika
verse_english: Dhp 17: Here he suffers, after death he suffers, the wicked one suffers in both places, he suffers, thinking: “I have done wickedness,” gone to a bad fate, he suffers much more.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Bāhiya Dārucīriya
synopsis: Bāhiya Dārucīriya obtained a short teaching from the Buddha, became an Arahat and died straight afterwards; the Buddha appointed him as foremost amongst those who were quick to grasp the teaching, and when the bhikkhus doubted it, he taught them with a verse. Buddhas
verse_english: Dhp 101: Though there are a thousand verses consisting of useless words, better is one word of a verse hearing which one is brought to peace.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa
synopsis: Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa took to storing up food so as not to be bothered with the almsround; the bhikkhus reported it to the Buddha, who laid down a rule forbidding the storing of food, and gave this teaching.
verse_english: Dhp 92: For those who have no stores, those who comprehend food aright, for those whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, their track is hard to find.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Elder Janapada Kaḷyāṇī Rūpanandā
synopsis: The Buddha caused Elder Rūpanandā, who was proud of her beauty, to see an image of a very beautiful woman quickly go through the stages of life, die, and be eaten by animals, and she gained insight into the nature of the body; the Buddha then spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 150: This fortress is made out of bones, plastered over with flesh and blood, but hidden within lie old age, death, also conceit and anger.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Weaver’s Daughter
synopsis: A weaver’s daughter heard the Buddha teach on contemplation of death and undertook the practice herself; after three years the Buddha returned to her home town and asked her four questions which she sagely answered, but no one understood her answers except the Buddha; he then spoke a verse, hearing which, she attained Stream-entry.
verse_english: Dhp 174: This world is blind, few here have true insight, as few go to heaven as birds that escape from the net.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Twin Miracle
synopsis: After spending his seventh Rains Retreat teaching the Abhidhamma in the Realm of the Thirty-Three, the Buddha descended on a staircase built by Sakka, the Lord of the Devas, and Elder Sāriputta praised the Buddha in his glory; the Buddha explained the matter by reciting a verse. Bimbisāra, King Pasenadi Kosala, Sakka, Gaṇḍa, Elder Ānanda, Devaputta Vātavalāhaka, Devaputta Sun, Pūraṇa Kassapa, Gharaṇī, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Mahā Brahma, Sāmaṇerī Cīrā, Sāmaṇera Cunda, Bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, Nandivisāla, Elder Anuruddha, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Deva Indaka, Deva Aṅkura, Buddha Kassapa, Deva Pañcasikha, Mātali the charioteer, Suyāma Lives, Previous Buddhas, Bodhisatta
verse_english: Dhp 181: Those wise ones intent on meditation, who delight in the peace of renunciation, even the gods are envious of them, the Sambuddhas, the ones who are mindful.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Edler Ānanda’s Question about the Observance Day
synopsis: Elder Ānanda asked the Buddha to explain how the previous Buddhas had kept the Observance Day; he explained that although they held them after different lengths of time, the verses they recited were always the same, and he recited them. Kakusandha, Buddha Koṇāgamana, Buddha Kassapa
verse_english: Dhp 183: The non-doing of anything wicked, undertaking of what is good, the purification of one’s mind - this is the teaching of the Buddhas. / Dhp 184: Enduring patience is the supreme austerity, Nibbāna is supreme say the Buddhas, for one gone forth does not hurt another, (nor does) an ascetic harass another. / Dhp 185: Not finding fault, not hurting, restraint by the regulations, knowing the right measure of food, (living in) a remote dwelling, devotion to meditation - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about a Son of a Wagon Driver
synopsis: A youth became very practised at the recollection of the Buddha, so when he was attacked by Amanussas he called out: ‘Homage to the Buddha’, which forced the Amanussas to serve him; when the king found out he asked the Buddha if only this recollection was an effective protection, and the Buddha taught six types of meditation.
verse_english: Dhp 296: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Buddha. / Dhp 297: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Dhamma. / Dhp 298: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Saṅgha. / Dhp 299: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the body. / Dhp 300: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night have a mind that delights in non-violence. / Dhp 301: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night have a mind that delights in cultivation.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about Udena
synopsis: King Udena had two queens, Sāmāvatī, who was a follower of the Buddha, and Māgandiyā, who was spurned by the Buddha; out of jealousy Māgandiyā brought about the destruction of Sāmāvatī and her five hundred followers, all of whom had attained stages of Awakening; Māgandiyā and her family, who were full of defilements, were put to death by the king; when what had happened was reported to the Buddha he spoke some verses about them.
verse_english: Dhp 21: Heedfulness is the deathless state, heedlessness the state of the dead, the heedful do not die, (but) those who are heedless are as if dead. / Dhp 22: The wise, understanding this difference in regard to heedfulness, rejoice in heedfulness, delight in the domain of the Noble Ones. / Dhp 23: Those who meditate all the time, constant and firm in their effort, those wise ones reach Nibbāna, the unsurpassed release from (all) bonds.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about a Certain Maiden of Family
synopsis: The Buddha and the monastics were invited to a wedding, and the bride served them with all due attention; the groom, however, was overcome with lust and could pay no attention to his duties; the Buddha spoke a verse to him.
verse_english: Dhp 202: There is no fire like passion, there is no offence like hatred, there is no suffering like the components (of mind and body), no happiness other than peace.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Novice Sumana
synopsis: Elder Anuruddha gave the young boy Sumana the going-forth and he soon became an Arahat; through his power the novice overcame a Nāga who then became his servant; when bhikkhus who did not know who he was started making fun of the novice the Buddha decided to let him demonstrate his power and sent him to Lake Anotatta in the Himalayas to bring water; the Buddha pointed him out flying through the air and spoke a verse. the Sakyan, Mahānāma, Elder Anuruddha, Mahā Muṇḍa, Mahā Sumana, Culla Sumana, Paṇṇaka, Sakka, Suyāma, Santusita, Paranimmitavasavattī, Elder Ānanda
verse_english: Dhp 382: That young monastic who is devoted to the Buddha’s dispensation, shines forth in this world, like the moon freed from a cloud.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Elder Who Meditated on a Mirage
synopsis: A bhikkhu who had been practising meditation saw a mirage, and realised this was similar to existence; he next saw froth on a river, with its bubbles bursting, and he realised existence is the same; the Buddha summed up his insight with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 46: Knowing that this body is just like froth, understanding it has the nature of a mirage, cutting off Māra’s flower-tipped (arrows), one should go beyond the King of Death’s sight.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Childless Rich Man
synopsis: In a previous life a rich man gave a meal to a Paccekabuddha but almost instantly regretted it; later, out of greed, he also killed his brother’s son; when reborn, because of his gift he was again rich, but because of his bad deed he was childless, lived as a miser and was unable to enjoy his riches; when he died all his wealth went to the king; the Buddha explained the situation with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 355: Riches destroy the stupid one who does not seek the way beyond, through his craving for riches the stupid one destroys others and himself.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about a Son of a Wagon Driver
synopsis: A youth became very practised at the recollection of the Buddha, so when he was attacked by Amanussas he called out: ‘Homage to the Buddha’, which forced the Amanussas to serve him; when the king found out he asked the Buddha if only this recollection was an effective protection, and the Buddha taught six types of meditation.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Selfish Kosiya
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna brought the miser Kosiya and his wife to the Buddha who taught them about generosity, and they both attained Stream-entry; the Buddha praised Elder Moggallāna for being both persuasive and modest with his supporters, and spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 49: Just as a bee, without hurting the flower, its colour or scent, gathers its nectar and escapes, so should the seer roam in the village.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about Prince Bodhi
synopsis: Prince Bodhi invited the Buddha for the first meal in his new palace, and put down cloth thinking if the Buddha stepped on it he would be blessed with children; the Buddha refused to walk on it, and explained that Prince Bodhi would be without children because of a past life in which he failed to protect himself by keeping precepts during any of the three periods of his life, and he then gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 157: If one regards oneself as dear one should guard oneself right well, during one of the three watches (of the night) the wise one should stay alert.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Old Brahmin’s Sons
synopsis: Some children who were previously negligent later gave a meal to the Buddha and the Saṅgha, and related how they now took care of their father; the Buddha recited a Birth Story relating how he too had cared for his parents, and spoke a verse showing how he would not eat until he was allowed to attend to his duties.
verse_english: Dhp 324: The tusker named Dhanapālaka musty in rut, difficult to restrain, bound, he doesn’t eat (even) a morsel, the tusker remembers the elephant forest.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Elder Mahā Moggallāna
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna was murdered by brigands acting on behalf of the naked ascetics; the Buddha explained that in a past life, being swayed by his wife he had murdered his parents, which was why he died in this way in the present life, and then he spoke some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 137: Whoever offends with a stick those who are inoffensive and harmless will quickly fall into one of ten states: / Dhp 138: harsh feelings, loss (of his wealth), and the break up of the body, or even heavy affliction, or surely he will lose his mind, / Dhp 139: (there may be) danger from the King, or slander that is terrible, (he may suffer from) loss of kin, or (from) the destruction of wealth, / Dhp 140: also his houses may be consumed by flames and fire, and at the break-up of the body that one lacking in wisdom will arise in the underworld.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse. Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Kokālika
verse_english: Dhp 17: Here he suffers, after death he suffers, the wicked one suffers in both places, he suffers, thinking: “I have done wickedness,” gone to a bad fate, he suffers much more.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍalakesī
synopsis: Kuṇḍalakesī, who had previously killed her husband and joined the wanderers and expertly defended their doctrines, was converted by Elder Sāriputta with a simple teaching; the bhikkhus wondered how, and the Buddha spoke some verses to explain it.
verse_english: Dhp 102: One may speak a hundred verses consisting of useless words, better is one verse of Dhamma, hearing which one is brought to peace. / Dhp 103: One may conquer a thousand men a thousand times in a battle, but having conquered one’s own self, one would surely be supreme in battle.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Wise Archer Culla Dhanuggaha
synopsis: When Elder Culla Dhanuggaha obtained water from the house of a young maiden she soon started giving him porridge also and striking up a conversation, and eventually he began to feel discontent; when the Buddha heard of the situation he described how this woman murdered him at the drop of a hat in a previous existence and further gave him a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 349: For a person crushed by thoughts and pierced by passion, contemplating the attractive, craving increases much more, this surely makes the bond more firm. / Dhp 350: Whoever has delight in the calming of thoughts, who always mindfully cultivates what is unattractive, will surely abolish this (craving), he will cut off the bond of Māra.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about a Certain Youth of Good Family
synopsis: A youth got married but his wife was given to adultery and put the young man to shame; when he met the Buddha the latter reminded him that in a previous existence also he was betrayed by his wife, and then he taught him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 242: Bad conduct is a woman’s stain, stinginess is a giver’s stain, wicked actions are indeed stains both in this world and in the next. / Dhp 243: A stain that is worse than that stain, ignorance is the supreme stain, after abandoning that stain, be without stains, O monastics!

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Woman Jealous by Nature
synopsis: A jealous woman found out her husband had been unfaithful with one of their maidservants, and had her nose and ears cut off, threw her into a dungeon and then went to listen to the Dhamma; one of her relatives discovered the matter and informed the Buddha, who gave the teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 314: Better undone is a wrong-doing, a wrong-doing one later regrets, better done is what is well-done, which, when done, one does not regret.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about Three Groups
synopsis: Three different groups of bhikkhus who were on their way to the Buddha saw a crow die in mid-air, a woman drowned on a voyage and themselves get buried in a cave; they asked the Buddha why it all happened, and he explained there is nowhere to escape from the results of bad actions, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 127: Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor after entering a mountain cleft: there is no place found on this earth where one can be free from (the results of) wicked deeds.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about Khema
synopsis: One of the merchant Anāthapiṇḍika’s nephews, Khema, was so handsome all the women fell in love with him, and he was frequently caught in adultery; the king didn’t punish Khema, due to his affection for his father, so his father took his son to the Buddha who taught him in some verses the destiny of those who dally with other men’s wives.
verse_english: Dhp 309: There are four states the man who is heedless, the man who consorts with other man’s wives, undergoes: he gains demerit, an uncomfortable bed, blame as third, and (rebirth in) the underworld as fourth. / Dhp 310: Gaining demerit and a bad destiny, and (only) the small delight of a scared man with a scared woman, and kings who apply heavy punishment, a man therefore should not consort with another’s wife.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
synopsis: A bhikkhu was given a subject of meditation, went to the forest, and became an Arahat; as he was travelling a woman who had quarrelled with her husband followed close behind; when the husband saw them he thrashed the bhikkhu; the bhikkhus could not believe he had not got angry with the man, but the Buddha confirmed his purity with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 405: * Whoever has laid down the stick (used) against fearful and fearless beings, who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a brahmin.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Defeat of the King of Kosala
synopsis: The King of Kosala is defeated three times by his nephew Ajātasattu, the King of Magadha, and took to his bed in sorrow and despair; when the Buddha heard about it he gave this teaching.
verse_english: Dhp 201: The victor generates hatred, the defeated one finds suffering, the one at peace lives happily, having abandoned victory and defeat.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta sought to kill the Buddha and take over the running of the Saṅgha; the Buddha explained that he also tried to kill him in other existences, but it all worked to Devadatta’s downfall, and then he spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 162: The one who has an exceeding lack of virtue, like a deadly creeper covering a Sal tree, makes himself the same as his enemy wishes him to be.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about the Elder Nigamavāsī Tissa
synopsis: Nigamavāsī Tissa lived near Sāvatthī and after he ordained he only went to his local village for alms; the bhikkhus blamed him but the Buddha praised him for being frugal and content, and spoke a verse praising his way of life.
verse_english: Dhp 32: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in heedlessness, is unable to fall away: he is well-nigh to Nibbāna.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about a Discontented Bhikkhu
synopsis: A bhikkhu had gained an inheritance of one hundred coins from his father and thought to return to the lay life; the Buddha pointed out that the money would not be enough to support himself, and related the Birth Story about Mandhātā which shows that no matter how much a person has he will never be satisfied.
verse_english: Dhp 186: Not through a rain of coins is satisfaction found for sense desires, the wise one knowing: “Sense pleasures have little joy, (much) suffering,” / Dhp 187: does not find delight even in heavenly pleasures. The disciple of the Perfect Sambuddha delights in craving’s destruction.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about Mahāli’s Questions
synopsis: Prince Magha did good works in his village and inspired thirty-three others to join him; later they were reborn as Sakka and his company of Thirty-three; the Buddha spoke a verse explaining what had happened.
verse_english: Dhp 30: Through heedfulness Maghavā attained leadership of the gods, (the good) praise heedfulness, (but) heedlessness is always blamed.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about Giving Alms to the Elder Mahā Kassapa
synopsis: Elder Mahā Kassapa rose from meditation after seven days and went for alms; celestial spirits stepped forward to donate to him but he dismissed them, then Sakka and his wife Sujā disguised themselves as weavers and succeeded in giving alms, but Elder Mahā Kassapa discovered who they were and chided them; the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 56: Pinwheel and sandalwood fragrance are insignificant, but the fragrance of one who has virtue flutters supreme amongst the gods.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about the Novice Paṇḍita
synopsis: The novice Paṇḍita saw that irrigators, fletchers and carpenters mastered the objects they worked with, and realised that if they can master unconscious things, he could master his mind; by striving he did just that and became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about him. Sāriputta
verse_english: Dhp 80: Course-makers lead water, fletchers straighten arrows, carpenters straighten wood, the wise master themselves.

question: Whose wife called after him, with her hair only half combed, asking him to come back soon, which later made him want to leave the monastery?
title: The Story about Kosambivāsī Tissa’s Novice
synopsis: Elder Tissa ordained a novice, who in the ordination hall became an Arahat; later they travelled, and through the carelessness of the bhikkhu the novice’s eye was put out; the novice, however, didn’t get angry but went about his duties as normal; the Buddha explained it with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 96: His mind is calm, his speech and his actions are also calm, liberated by right knowledge, such a one is (truly) peaceful.

question: Whose wife called after him, with her hair only half combed, asking him to come back soon, which later made him want to leave the monastery?
title: The Story about the Elder Cittahattha
synopsis: Cittahattha wavered continually between being a bhikkhu and a householder, but eventually he saw into the truth of impermanence, ordained yet again and became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 38: For the one with unsettled mind, who does not know the True Dhamma, whose confidence is wavering, wisdom is unfulfilled. / Dhp 39: For the one with mind free of lust, for the one with mind unperplexed, for the one who has abandoned making merit and demerit, for the watchful, there is no fear.

title: The Story about a Company of Bhikkhus
synopsis: After Soṇa Kūṭikaṇṇa received ordination he recited Dhamma to the Buddha who praised him for it, which also caused the Devas to rejoice; on hearing about it, Soṇa’s mother invited her son to teach her Dhamma also, and wouldn’t leave the teaching even when she heard nine hundred thieves had broken into her house; seeing her piety, the thieves converted and went forth; this is the teaching the Buddha gave at that time.
verse_english: Dhp 368: That monastic who dwells in loving-kindness, with faith in Buddha’s dispensation, should attain the state of peace, the joy in stilling of (all) conditions. / Dhp 369: Please bail out this boat, monastic, when bailed out it will go lightly, cutting off passion and hatred, from here one will go to Nibbāna. / Dhp 370: One should cut off five, one should abandon five, one should cultivate five more, the monastic who surmounts five attachments is called a flood-crosser. / Dhp 371: Meditate, monastic, do not be heedless, do not let your mind swirl around in strands of desire, do not, heedless, swallow a (hot) iron ball, do not, while burning, cry: ‘This is suffering.’ / Dhp 372: There is no concentration for one without wisdom, there is no wisdom for one without concentration, the one who has both concentration and wisdom is indeed in the presence of Nibbāna. / Dhp 373: For the one who has entered an empty place, a monastic with a peaceful mind, there is superhuman delight from insight into true Dhamma. / Dhp 374: Whoever has right mindfulness regarding the rise and fall of the components (of mind and body) gains joy and happiness, that is the deathless state for the one who knows. / Dhp 375: This is the very beginning for the wise monastic here: contentment, guarding the senses, and restraint in the regulations. / Dhp 376: One should resort to spiritual friends, ones of pure life, ones who are diligent, one should be of friendly disposition, one who will be skilful in his conduct, rejoicing frequently because of that, one will make an end to suffering.

title: The Story about the Young Sow
synopsis: One day the Buddha saw a sow and smiled; when Elder Ānanda asked him the reason for his smile he told of the various forms of existence that the sow had been through, including being reborn in the Brahma worlds in the life before this one; he then taught the monastics on the wickedness of craving with some verses. title: The Story about the Four Novices
synopsis: A Brahmin’s wife sought for four Brahmins to give a meal to and was sent the four Arahat novices Saṁkicca, Paṇḍita, Sopāka and Revata, whom she sat on the floor and would not serve; being alerted, Sakka came and convinced her to serve them; the bhikkhus could not believe the novices had not got angry with the woman, but the Buddha confirmed their purity with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 406: Being friendly with the hostile, calm amongst those holding a stick, not attached amongst those attached, that one I say is a brahmin.

title: The Story about the Elder Soreyya
synopsis: A merchant’s son, Soreyya, developed lust for Elder Mahā Kaccāyana and was transformed into a woman; later, after asking pardon, he became a man again, ordained and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha explained what a well-directed mind can do for one.
verse_english: Dhp 43: Mother and father might not do for him, or other relatives, as much good as a mind that is well-directed can do for him.

title: The Story about the Elder Revata
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta’s youngest brother Revata escaped from the household life and became a bhikkhu, and soon after became an Arahat; after the Rains Retreat the Buddha visited him, and by psychic power Elder Revata transformed the thorn thickets he lived in into something well-equipped and quite delightful; the bhikkhus proclaimed his merit, but the Buddha explained the elder has overcome all merit and demerit and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 412: Whoever here has overcome clinging to both merit and demerit, who is griefless, dustless and pure, that one I say is a brahmin.

question: On one evening Ānanda watched the sun going down, the moon coming up, the king in his finery and a monk meditating. What did the Buddha say shone brightest?
title: The Story about the Bhikkhus Who Lived on the Banks of the Vaggumudā
synopsis: The bhikkhus who lived on the banks of the Vaggumudā went around praising each other and saying they had attained states they had not in order to get better almsfood; the Buddha restrained those bhikkhus and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 308: It’s better to have eaten a glowing iron ball, like a flame of fire, than that (the monastic) who is unrestrained and unvirtuous should enjoy the country’s almsfood.

question: On one evening Ānanda watched the sun going down, the moon coming up, the king in his finery and a monk meditating. What did the Buddha say shone brightest?
title: The Story about the Elder Mahā Kappina
synopsis: Elder Mahā Kappina, who was formerly a king, was given to exclaiming his delight, and the bhikkhus feared he was recalling the joys he had when king; the Buddha explained the true reason for his exclamations was delight in the Dhamma, and spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 79: The one who drinks Dhamma lives well, with a clear mind, the wise one will always delight in the Dhamma that is made known by the Noble.

question: On one evening Ānanda watched the sun going down, the moon coming up, the king in his finery and a monk meditating. What did the Buddha say shone brightest?
title: The Story about the Elder Ānanda
synopsis: One day Elder Ānanda saw the sun set, the moon rise, the king in his mantle, Elder Kāḷudāyi meditating and the Buddha, who outshone them all; the Teacher explained that Buddhas outshine the others both by day and by night, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 387: The sun is radiant by day, the moon shines by night, the accoutred noble is radiant, the meditating brahmin is radiant, yet every day and night the Buddha is radiant through his power.

title: The Story about the Novice Sukha
synopsis: The novice Sukha saw that irrigators, fletchers and carpenters mastered the objects they worked with, and realised that, if they can master unconscious things, he could master his mind; he asked his teacher Elder Sāriputta to bring his food, and by striving alone he became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about him. Disciples, Mastery, Past Lives
verse_english: Dhp 145: Course-makers lead water, fletchers straighten arrows, carpenters straighten wood, the mild master themselves.

title: The Story about the Elder Sammuñjani
synopsis: Elder Sammuñjani spent all his time sweeping the monastery and never meditated, but Elder Revata admonished him to spend some time in meditation, which he did and he became an Arahat; the Buddha confirmed to the bhikkhu his attainment and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 172: Whoever was heedless before, but later is not heedless, that one shines brightly on this world like the moon released from a cloud.

title: The Story about the Exalted Utterances (Spoken) to Elder Ānanda
synopsis: After he had defeated Māra at the foot of the Bodhi tree, the Bodhisatta, in the three watches of the night, attained insight into his previous existences, the rising and falling away of beings according to their intentional actions, and dependent origination, which led to his Awakening, at which point he spoke exalted utterances.
verse_english: Dhp 153: Through the round of countless births and deaths I have wandered without finding the housebuilder I was seeking: born and suffering once again. / Dhp 154: O housebuilder, now you are seen! You will not build the house again: all your rafters have been broken, and the ridgepole has been destroyed, my mind has reached the unconditioned, and craving’s end has been achieved.

title: The Story about the Edler Ānanda’s Question about the Observance Day
synopsis: Elder Ānanda asked the Buddha to explain how the previous Buddhas had kept the Observance Day; he explained that although they held them after different lengths of time, the verses they recited were always the same, and he recited them. Kakusandha, Buddha Koṇāgamana, Buddha Kassapa
verse_english: Dhp 183: The non-doing of anything wicked, undertaking of what is good, the purification of one’s mind - this is the teaching of the Buddhas. / Dhp 184: Enduring patience is the supreme austerity, Nibbāna is supreme say the Buddhas, for one gone forth does not hurt another, (nor does) an ascetic harass another. / Dhp 185: Not finding fault, not hurting, restraint by the regulations, knowing the right measure of food, (living in) a remote dwelling, devotion to meditation - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

title: The Story about the Elder Culla Panthaka
synopsis: When Elder Culla Panthaka could not remember even four lines of verse after three months trying, the Buddha asked him to rub a white cloth, which subsequently became soiled and gave him initial insight into impermanence; the Buddha then taught him that the mind is also defiled and must be cleansed, and he soon attained deliverance, after which the Buddha spoke a verse about him. verse_english: Dhp 25: Through activity, heedfulness, through self-control and through restraint, the sage should make an island that no flood waters can overcome.

synopsis: Queen Māgandiyā, who had been rejected by the Buddha, bribed the crowd and slaves to abuse him and the bhikkhus when they came to town; Elder Ānanda urged the Buddha to go elsewhere but the Buddha answered that they should be resolute and spoke about himself in these verses.

verse_english: Dhp 94: For the one whose senses are stilled, like horses well-trained by their charioteer, who has abandoned conceit, who is without pollutants – even the gods envy such a one.

synopsis: A barren woman brings home a young woman for her husband, but every time the young wife conceives the barren wife contrives an abortion; through life after life they consume each other’s children, until brought to the Buddha, who taught them with a verse. named, Elder Ānanda, Deva Sumana
verse_english: Dhp 5: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place, they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is (surely) eternal.

synopsis: King Pasenadi was overcome with desire for another man’s wife and sought to have him killed; during the night he woke to the sound of four people screaming; the Buddha explained they were adulterers in their previous lives and did no good deeds, and then he spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 60: Long is the night for one awake, long is a league for one tired, long is the round of births and deaths for fools who know not True Dhamma.

title: The Story about the Lay Disciple Mahā Kāla
synopsis: The householder Mahā Kāla listened to an all-night Dhamma teaching at Jetavana, but in the morning was beaten to death by people who mistook him for a thief; the Buddha explained that he had caused the unjust death of another in a previous life, and his bad deed had caught up with him, and gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 161: That wickedness done by oneself, born in oneself, arising in oneself, crushes the one who is stupid, as a diamond (crushes) a rock-jewel.

synopsis: One of the merchant Anāthapiṇḍika’s nephews, Khema, was so handsome all the women fell in love with him, and he was frequently caught in adultery; the king didn’t punish Khema, due to his affection for his father, so his father took his son to the Buddha who taught him in some verses the destiny of those who dally with other men’s wives.
verse_english: Dhp 309: There are four states the man who is heedless, the man who consorts with other man’s wives, undergoes: he gains demerit, an uncomfortable bed, blame as third, and (rebirth in) the underworld as fourth. / Dhp 310: Gaining demerit and a bad destiny, and (only) the small delight of a scared man with a scared woman, and kings who apply heavy punishment, a man therefore should not consort with another’s wife.

verse_english: Dhp 326: Formerly this wandering mind wandered through desire, pleasure and happiness, (but) today I will control it wisely, like one with goad an elephant in rut.

verse_english: Dhp 35: * For the mind that is difficult to subdue, flighty, flitting wherever it will, restraint is good, a restrained mind brings happiness.

verse_english: Dhp 100: Though there are a thousand sayings consisting of useless words, better is one useful word hearing which one is brought to peace.

synopsis: The bhikkhus did not want to ordain a poor Brahmin, Rādha, but the Buddha, seeing his potential, allowed it; Elder Sāriputta gave him guidance which he followed to the letter and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about being amenable to admonition.
verse_english: Dhp 76: One should regard someone who shows your faults just like one who points out hidden treasure, one should keep company with such a sagacious, learned person who reproves you; keeping company with such is (surely) better for you, not worse.

synopsis: The lay disciple Atula went with his entourage to see Elder Revata, who did not speak; Elder Sāriputta, who spoke at length; and Elder Ānanda who spoke moderately; but he was upset with them all; finally he went to the Buddha who explained the matter with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 227: This is something of old, Atula, this is not something of today: they blame the one who sits silently, they blame the one who talks a lot, they blame the one who talks in moderation, there is no one in the world not blamed. / Dhp 228: There was not and there will not be, and at present there is not found a person totally blameworthy, or one totally praiseworthy. / Dhp 229: The one who, after being examined day by day, is praised by the wise, faultless in conduct, sagacious, attending to virtue and wisdom, / Dhp 230: one who is like a golden coin, who is there worthy to blame him? verse_english: Dhp 72: As far as learning arises for a fool, it is only to his disadvantage, it destroys the fool’s good fortune, and it will destroy his head.

synopsis: The bhikkhu Cakkhupāla determined to fulfil his practice even at the cost of his eyes, and eventually he attained Awakening; the Buddha explained the deed he did in the past which caused his loss of sight in the present, and he summarised the teaching with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 1: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind, if with a base mind one speaks or acts, through that suffering follows him like a wheel (follows) the ox’s foot.

title: The Story about the Elder Dhammika

verse_english: Dhp 84: Not for one’s own sake and not for another’s sake, not desiring a child, riches, or a kingdom – he should not desire his success through corruption; he should be both virtuous and wise and righteous.

question: Why am I blind to my own shortcomings yet quick to judge everybody else?
title: The Story about the Sectarian Disciples
synopsis: Some children of the families of sectarians were forbidden to go to Jetavana, but when thirst overtook them one day they went anyway; the Buddha gave them an appropriate teaching and they converted; later they went to the monastery to ordain and the Buddha taught them with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 318: Finding blame in what is blameless, not seeing blame in what is blameable, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny. / Dhp 319: Knowing blame in what is blameable, and no blame in what is blameless, undertaking right views, beings go to a good destiny.

question: Why am I blind to my own shortcomings yet quick to judge everybody else?
title: The Story about the Elder Ujjhānasaññī
synopsis: Elder Ujjhānasaññī was always finding fault with the others, so the bhikkhus asked the Buddha about it; he remarked that one who is scrupulous is doing well, but one who enjoys finding fault, makes no progress, and he taught them with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 253: The one who constantly looks for another’s fault, who is an abject complainer, for him the pollutants increase, he is far from their destruction.

question: Why am I blind to my own shortcomings yet quick to judge everybody else?
title: The Story about the Nigaṇṭhas
synopsis: Some bhikkhus saw the Nigaṇṭhas and spoke of them as having some modesty as they wear a small covering at the front, the Nigaṇṭhas however declared they do so not out of modesty, but to protect the lives of dust-beings; when reported to the Buddha he spoke a verse about them.
verse_english: Dhp 316: They are ashamed of what is not shameful, not ashamed of what is shameful, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny. / Dhp 317: Seeing fear in what is not fearful, not seeing fear in what is fearful, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

question: Why am I blind to my own shortcomings yet quick to judge everybody else?
title: The Story about the Rich Man Meṇḍaka
synopsis: The rich man Meṇḍaka wanted to see the Buddha when he was passing through, but the outside ascetics tried to persuade him not to by telling him falsely that he teaches there is no result of actions; Meṇḍaka went anyway and the Buddha taught him with a verse. Vipassī, Avaroja
verse_english: Dhp 252: Easy to see are others’ fault, but one’s own is hard to see, for one sifts other people’s faults like they were chaff, but conceals one’s own (faults), like a crafty cheat (conceals) his defeat.

verse_english: Dhp 6: The others do not understand that we should restrain ourselves here, but (for) those here who do understand, through that, (their) dissensions will cease.

synopsis: When the Buddha lay ill Sakka, Lord of the Gods, came to attend to him; the bhikkhus wondered why, and the Buddha explained how he had previously answered Sakka’s questions who thereby became a Stream-enterer; the Buddha summarised Sakka’s affection with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 206: Meeting with the noble is good, living together (with them) is always pleasant, through not meeting foolish people one will constantly be happy. / Dhp 207: For he who consorts with fools grieves for a long time, dwelling with fools is always suffering as it is with enemies, the wise one dwells happily as with an assembly of kin. / Dhp 208: therefore, the firm, the wise and the learned, the virtuous, dutiful and noble – * (accompany) such a true and intelligent person as the moon accompanies the course of the stars.

verse_english: Dhp 119: Even the wicked one experiences good fortune while the wickedness does not ripen, but when the wickedness ripens then the wicked one experiences wicked things. / Dhp 120: Even the fortunate one experiences wickedness as long as the good fortune does not ripen, but when the fortune ripens then the fortunate one experiences good fortune.

question: What does it count as good fortune, such as having companions when you are in trouble?
title: The Story about Māra
synopsis: The Buddha was reflecting on whether it is possible for kings to rule the world with justice; Māra, finding this out, came to the wrong conclusion, and tried to tempt him; the Buddha explained what is truly good with some verses.

question: What does it count as good fortune, such as having companions when you are in trouble?
title: The Story about a Company of Bhikkhus
synopsis: Owing to the Kosambī bhikkhus falling into an argument, the Buddha went to Pārileyyaka forest and was served by an elephant; after the Rains Retreat Elder Ānanda, being urged by the great disciples, went to invite the Buddha to return to Sāvatthi; the Buddha explained that he had a good companion in the elephant, but without such-like it is better to live alone, and he spoke some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 328: If you should find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, overcoming all your troubles you should live with that one, glad and mindful. / Dhp 329: If you do not find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, like a king who abandons his conquered kingdom one should live alone like a solitary elephant in the forest. / Dhp 330: It is better to live alone, there can be no friendship with a fool, one should live alone and not do anything bad, unconcerned like a solitary elephant in the forest.

synopsis: Elder Poṭhila had been a reciter of the Three Baskets under all seven Buddhas, but had never truly put the teaching into practice, so the Buddha started calling him Empty Poṭhila; taking the hint he went far away to practice meditation, and later the Buddha appeared to him and spoke a verse to encourage him.

verse_english: Dhp 405: * Whoever has laid down the stick (used) against fearful and fearless beings, who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a brahmin.

verse_english: Dhp 391: For whom there is no wrong-doing bodily, verbally or mentally, being restrained in (these) three things, that one I say is a brahmin.

question: What is said about someone who never harms any creature, weak or strong, and never gets others to do it?
title: The Story about the Fisherman Named Ariya

question: Explain arogya parama labha, santutthi paramam dhanam.

synopsis: King Pasenadi was always overeating and suffering for it so the Buddha had the king’s nephew learn and recite a verse which reminded the king to be moderate; later the king told the Buddha he was cured, and the Buddha recited a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 204: Health is the supreme gain, content the supreme wealth, confidence the supreme kin, Nibbāna the supreme good.
